subject: Reserved commit — modular bundles & start-gate alignment
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@stratusai.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved commit questions + MAUP attached

Jonas / team,

Thanks for the demo last week — StratusAI is seriously evaluating Redwood for a production migration in Q4. Before we proceed to procurement, we need to firm up a few items on the reserved commit side so our finance and infra teams can model the cashflow and deployment plan: 

- Term options: we prefer to see firm pricing for 12 / 24 / 36 month commits. Can you include both list price and an illustrative discount matrix (we typically anchor to 36-mo).
- Start gate: our legal wants clarity on what constitutes an "activation" window. We need a guaranteed latest-capacity start date (we'd like no later than Aug 1, 2027) or a credit/penalty mechanism if start slips.
- Ramp cadence: outline a realistic ramp schedule (weeks to reach 80% throughput) for a 500-A100-equivalent pool.
- Throughput SLA / fallback: if you can't meet committed throughput, what are the guaranteed remedies (credits, burst access, downgrade to compatible model variants)?

I've attached our MAUP and procurement constraints (stratusai_maup_v3.xlsx). Please loop in pricing and legal — procurement@stratusai.com is on cc.

Appreciate a concise proposal; procurement is targeting a final term decision by end of April.

— Liam
Liam O'Neill
VP of Infrastructure, StratusAI
liam.oneill@stratusai.com

Attachments: stratusai_maup_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@stratusai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved commit questions + MAUP attached

Thanks Liam — great to hear StratusAI is moving toward production. I pulled pricing and infra into this thread and sketched a concise approach below. High level proposal (we'll formalize in a short-term SOW / commercial addendum):

1) Modular reserve bundles (flexible packaging)
   - Base reserved commit: choose 12 / 24 / 36 month term at a base vCPU/GPU-equivalent price.
   - Add-on buckets: smaller burst buckets that can be used for short-term peak traffic (metered at a blended higher rate).
   - Soft-start credits: the first 60 days include a "soft-start" token pool (credits) to accommodate slower-than-expected production ramp.

2) Start gate and start date guarantee
   - We propose a contractual "Start Window": customer must begin capacity consumption within 60 days of contract signature (signature = countersigned agreement).
   - If Redwood cannot satisfy capacity by the agreed latest date (we can specify Aug 1, 2027 here), we provide either: (a) pro-rated service credits against committed fees for the impacted period, or (b) a temporary burst allocation at no additional cost until capacity is available.

3) Ramp schedule (for a 500-A100-equivalent pool) — conservative estimate
   - Week 0–2: provisioning and kernel optimization (20% throughput)
   - Week 3–6: KV-cache warm and batching profiles tuned (50–75%)
   - Week 7–10: sustained 80–95% throughput under config parity tests
   - We guarantee 80% baseline throughput by week 10, with documented telemetry hooks for visibility.

4) Throughput SLA & fallback
   - Throughput guarantee: 99.5% of tokens processed at agreed per-request latency during normal operating hours (or provide defined credit ladder if missed).
   - Fallbacks: automatic routing to a compatible model variant or an adjacent regional pool; bursts charged to burst buckets.

Pricing pointer (illustrative, final to be in commercial addendum):
   - 12-month: $X / GPU-equivalent-month (list) — minimal discount
   - 24-month: ~12% off list
   - 36-month: ~20% off list (anchor) + additional credits for earlier signature

I attached a short draft attachment (proposed_commit_terms_v2.pdf) and a spreadsheet with tier math. Ben / Rachel — please review the start-window language and confirm the credit mechanics and any required legal guardrails.

Next steps: if this aligns we can produce a one-page term sheet + SOW and get a DocuSign going. Liam — can you confirm the internal signatory and whether Aug 1 is a firm latest-start requirement?

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed_commit_terms_v2.pdf (document, 18KB), https://hubspot.example/record/HS-72198

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Proposed discount ladder + start-gate fallback language

Jonas / Rachel — quick internal note before we finalize the term sheet for StratusAI: 

- Discount ladder: I recommend we anchor the commercial discussion to the 36-mo for negotiation leverage; offer a 20% off list for 36, 12% for 24, and 5% for 12. Tie the deeper discount to two contract conditions: (1) fixed start-gate (no later than Aug 1, 2027) and (2) minimum early-payment schedule (quarterly).
- Start-gate fallback: prefer to default to a burst allocation as the primary remedy (reduces invoice reconciliation complexity), with a secondary service credit if burst capacity materially degrades performance. Keep credit caps (e.g., max 10% of monthly committed fee) to protect Redwood.
- Early termination: include a reduced termination fee if Stratus converts to a Dedicated-to-Private migration (we'll want to keep a path for long-term partnership).

I'll draft the contractual wording for the start window and credit ladder; Rachel — can you scope the telemetry / SLO reporting clauses we'll need to include in the SOW?

— Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@stratusai.com>

Cc: procurement@stratusai.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved commit questions + MAUP attached

On Tue, Apr 13, 2027 at 10:40 AM Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Liam — great to hear StratusAI is moving toward production. I pulled pricing and infra into this thread and sketched a concise approach below...

Jonas / Ben — thanks for the clear proposal and options. StratusAI's procurement reviewed the modular bundle construct and the start-window approach. A few confirmations and asks before we lock the term: 

- Start date: Aug 1, 2027 is acceptable as the latest-capacity start date. We will accept a soft-start credit structure if Redwood misses the date, but procurement prefers a capped credit (not a full refund) and a short-term burst while Redwood remedies capacity.
- Term: we want the 36-month anchor. Please provide final numbers for the 36-mo anchored price (incl. unit price and effective blended discount) and the exact credit cap wording.
- Ramp: the week 7–10 80% baseline looks reasonable — please include a short annex with the telemetry events you will publish and the format (prometheus / cloudwatch).

Procurement also needs DocuSign-ready term sheet and a standard PO flow (we use DocuSign then standard Net-45). I've attached our procurement policy for completion.

If you can get the one-page term sheet plus the SOW annex by end of day Wednesday (21 Apr), procurement will route internally and target signature the following week. Can you confirm?

— Liam
Liam O'Neill
VP of Infrastructure, StratusAI

Attachments: procurement_policy_procurement_v2.pdf (PDF, 26KB)
